title: Model Update and Rollback Lifecycle
summary: Plan, qualify, release, observe, and reverse model-serving changes without losing exact identity, compatibility, learner evidence, or a known-good recovery path.
objectives: Inventory every model, runtime, adapter, configuration, infrastructure, policy, and data dependency that can change serving behavior.
Build a compatibility manifest and qualify the exact candidate stack against quality, safety, security, capacity, cost, and recovery gates.
Choose a controlled rollout strategy with explicit observation windows, stop conditions, approvals, and immutable evidence.
Execute and verify rollback to a retained known-good stack, including schema and state compatibility.

sections.title: Version the entire serving unit
paragraphs: A model update is rarely only a weights change. Record the immutable model revision and digest together with tokenizer, runtime, accelerator libraries, container image, adapters, prompt templates, safety policy, gateway contract, infrastructure configuration, evaluation set, and telemetry schema. A change to any one of these can alter quality, latency, memory use, security, or compatibility.

Give the assembled candidate one release identity and produce a difference report against the currently approved stack. Separate intentional changes from drift. If the operator cannot reconstruct both versions from retained manifests and artifacts, the proposed release is not reversible.

sections.title: Qualify the exact candidate before traffic
paragraphs: Verify artifact provenance, license disposition, signatures or documented alternatives, dependency inventory, vulnerability findings, configuration policy, and environment compatibility. Then run the same representative quality, safety, API compatibility, load, cost, failure, and recovery tests used to approve the current build.

Compare candidate and baseline by case and operational slice rather than accepting one average. Define hard failures, allowed deltas, uncertainty, reviewer roles, and waiver authority before observing results. A newer model name does not override a failed compatibility or safety gate.

sections.title: Stage and release with bounded exposure
paragraphs: Choose a strategy that matches the environment and risk: offline replacement for a workstation, a second container and explicit route switch, rolling replacement, canary traffic, blue-green service, or a shadow comparison that cannot create user-visible effects. Preserve exact request routing and model identity in telemetry.

Define maximum exposure, observation window, success indicators, guardrail indicators, cost ceiling, approver, and automatic or manual stop conditions. Validate readiness and warm-up before admitting traffic, drain old capacity deliberately, and prevent mixed versions from silently invalidating evidence.

sections.title: Treat rollback as a tested release
paragraphs: Rollback must restore a complete compatible serving unit, not merely change a model tag. Retain the known-good artifacts, manifests, secrets references, policy, infrastructure configuration, and deployment procedure. Identify forward-only schema or state changes and provide restore, compatibility, or compensating procedures.

Rehearse rollback before production release using the same authorization, artifact verification, readiness, routing, and postcondition checks as an update. After reversal, confirm exact model identity, representative quality, endpoint behavior, queue state, telemetry, cost, and user-visible recovery.

sections.title: Close the lifecycle with evidence
paragraphs: Record who proposed, reviewed, approved, executed, paused, rolled back, and verified the change; retain timestamps, versions, test outputs, traffic exposure, decisions, and residual risks without storing secrets or unnecessary request content. Link every decision to immutable evidence.

Use release and rollback results to update evaluation cases, thresholds, capacity assumptions, compatibility manifests, and runbooks. Keep failed candidates as evidence with an explicit status so the same unsafe combination is not rediscovered and released later.

activity.title: Plan and rehearse a reversible model update
instructions: Create baseline and candidate manifests that identify the model, tokenizer, runtime, image, adapters, policies, configuration, evaluation set, and telemetry schema by immutable version.
Define quality, safety, security, compatibility, capacity, cost, and recovery comparisons with hard gates and authorized reviewers.
Select a workstation, container, on-premises, edge, or cloud rollout pattern and specify exposure, observation, stop, drain, and approval controls.
Run a tabletop or isolated rehearsal in which a guardrail fails, execute the rollback, and verify the restored endpoint and evidence.
Issue a release, reject, or revise decision and record the residual risks and required follow-up.
evidence: A baseline-to-candidate compatibility manifest and immutable difference report.
A gated qualification report and bounded rollout plan with human approvals.
Rollback rehearsal output proving restored identity, behavior, telemetry, and service objectives.

instructorScript.transcript: Version the complete serving unit because weights, runtime, adapters, policy, configuration, and infrastructure can all change behavior. Put the model revision, tokenizer, runtime, image, prompts, safety controls, infrastructure, evaluation set, and telemetry contract under one immutable release identity. Compare the exact candidate with the approved baseline across quality, safety, security, compatibility, capacity, cost, and recovery gates. Define hard failures and reviewer authority before looking at results. Bound traffic exposure, observation, cost, stopping, warm-up, routing, draining, and approval before starting the rollout. Preserve exact routing evidence so mixed versions cannot hide a regression. Rehearse rollback as a complete release and verify identity, behavior, state, telemetry, and user-visible recovery. Restoring a tag without restoring compatible dependencies is not a rollback. Preserve decision evidence and feed release results back into evaluations, thresholds, manifests, and runbooks. A failed candidate remains useful evidence when its status and exact composition are recorded.

questions.prompt: What belongs in the versioned serving unit?
choices: The model, tokenizer, runtime, image, adapters, policies, configuration, infrastructure, evaluations, and telemetry contract
questions.explanation: Every listed dependency can change behavior or prevent exact reconstruction.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest candidate qualification comparison?
choices: Candidate versus baseline by representative case and operational slice
questions.explanation: Case- and slice-level comparison exposes regressions hidden by averages.

questions.prompt: Why preserve exact routing identity during a canary?
choices: To attribute quality and operational outcomes to the actual version served
questions.explanation: A canary is only measurable when requests and outcomes map to an exact build.

questions.prompt: Which event should stop a rollout?
choices: An approved hard safety gate fails
questions.explanation: Predefined hard failures must stop exposure regardless of novelty.

choices: Restoring and verifying the complete compatible known-good serving unit and state
questions.explanation: Rollback must recover the whole compatible system and prove its postconditions.

questions.prompt: What should happen to evidence from a rejected candidate?
choices: Retain its exact identity, failed gates, disposition, and follow-up under policy
questions.explanation: Retained rejection evidence prevents unsafe combinations from being reconsidered without context.
